7 DRUG INTERACTIONS Strong CYP2D6 Inhibitors: Increased exposure of pitolisant tablets; reduce the maximum recommended dose of pitolisant tablets by half ( 2.6 , 7.1 ) Strong CYP3A4 Inducers: Decreased exposure of pitolisant tablets; consider dosage adjustment of pitolisant tablets ( 2.6 , 7.1 ).
Avoid coadministration of GAVRETO with a strong or moderate CYP3A and/or P-gp inhibitor.
The concomitant use of dextroamphetamine sulfate tablets and serotonergic drugs increases the risk of serotonin syndrome.

Concomitant administration of potassium citrate and a potassium-sparing diuretic (such as triamterene, spironolactone or amiloride) should be avoided since the simultaneous administration of these agents can produce severe hyperkalemia.
Avoid concomitant strong CYP3A4 inducers during abiraterone acetate treatment.

In a dedicated drug interaction trial, co-administration of ketoconazole, a strong inhibitor of CYP3A4, had no clinically meaningful effect on the pharmacokinetics of abiraterone [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ] .
Based on these results, fidaxomicin may be co-administered with P-gp inhibitors and no dose adjustment is recommended.
Combined P-gp and Strong CYP3A Inhibitors : Monitor patients more frequently for NUBEQA adverse reactions.
Use caution with concomitant use of moderate CYP3A inhibitors.
Avoid concomitant use of XOSPATA with combined P-gp and strong CYP3A inducers.
